title: Union Health Ministry’s Health Pavilion Records Around 1.5 Lakh Footfall at IITF 2026, Promotes ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’ through Preventive Healthcare and Healthy Living
subtitle:
Visitors Access Free Health Screenings, Diagnostic Tests, Medical Consultations and Counselling on Physical and Mental Health
Ayushman Arogya Mandir Stall Showcases Comprehensive Primary Healthcare Services, Emphasising Early Detection, Prevention and Accessible Care
Digital Health Initiatives, Including ABHA, eSanjeevani, U-WIN and Tele-MANAS, Familiarise Visitors with Technology-enabled Healthcare Services
Live CPR Demonstrations, TB Awareness Street Plays, Doctors’ Talk Shows and Interactive Activities Promote Health Awareness and Preventive Practices
Dedicated Kids’ Zone Promotes Physical Activity, Screen-free Recreation and Healthy Habits Among Children
Health Pavilion Observes Constitution Day with Collective Reading of the Preamble, Reaffirming Commitment to Constitutional Values
body_text: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s Health Pavilion recorded a footfall of around 1.5 lakh during the India International Trade Fair (IITF) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Children, young people and families visited the pavilion to access free health services, interact with healthcare professionals and learn about Government health programmes. Themed ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’, the pavilion promoted preventive healthcare and healthy everyday habits through interactive exhibits, live demonstrations and on-site services. The pavilion was inaugurated by Dr. M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog, in the presence of Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary. The Health Pavilion brought together 39 stalls representing 24 National Health Programmes, Programme Divisions and participating organisations, providing visitors an opportunity to learn about Government health initiatives and access a wide range of public health services. Ayushman Arogya Mandir Stall Highlights Preventive and Primary Healthcare A key attraction was the Ayushman Arogya Mandir stall, where visitors accessed basic health screenings and received guidance on preventive care. The stall familiarised visitors with the primary healthcare services available at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in their communities and encouraged them to make regular health check-ups part of their routine. Visitors Access Free Health Screenings, Tests and Consultations Across the pavilion, visitors accessed free services including BMI assessment, blood sugar testing, blood grouping, eye check-ups, oral health screenings and hearing assessments. They also received counselling on mental health, nutrition and tobacco cessation, along with guidance on maternal and child health, immunisation and disease prevention. Visitors learned how to access eSanjeevani teleconsultations, create an ABHA ID and check their eligibility for Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY). Participating stalls also familiarised visitors with the U-WIN vaccination platform and TeleMANAS mental health support services. Live Demonstrations and Interactive Activities Promote Health Awareness Live cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) demonstrations introduced visitors to essential emergency response skills. Street plays under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan highlighted the importance of recognising symptoms and seeking timely diagnosis and treatment. Doctors’ talk shows, interactive quizzes, magic shows and activities on vector-borne diseases offered visitors opportunities to ask questions and learn about preventive health practices. Dedicated Kids’ Zone Encourages Healthy Habits Through Play A dedicated Kids’ Zone was set up to engage children through traditional games and recreational activities. The initiative promoted screen-free engagement, physical activity and social interaction, while encouraging children to develop healthy habits through play and offering families an enjoyable experience at the Pavilion. Health Pavilion Observes Constitution Day On Constitution Day, participants at the Health Pavilion came together for a collective reading of the Preamble to the Constitution of India, reaffirming their commitment to the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. The Health Pavilion brought together free health services, information on national health programmes and interactive awareness activities, enabling visitors to engage directly with the Government’s public healthcare initiatives. Through its theme ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’, the pavilion reinforced the importance of preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and greater public participation in building a healthier nation. ***** SR HFW/MoHFW’s Health Pavilion Records Around 1.5 Lakh Footfall at IITF 2026/28 th November 2026/1
